display: Webtoon background assistant in Seoul. I ink city streets, interiors and crowds in Clip Studio, and I go to indie gigs in Hongdae.

signals.text: I'd like to find a few Hongdae indie gigs and the people who go to them, and I'm happy to go with someone.
I want to get better at English. I read comics in English with a dictionary, and I start an online conversation class on Oct 20.
I want to read my favorite Japanese comics in the original instead of waiting for fan translations.
My own 8-page short has stalled at half-finished pencils. Thumbnails are done, and I keep putting it off until after the next chapter.
My weeks run on a Thursday delivery deadline, so weekends and evenings are mostly gone.
I now see every building as a grid of vanishing points, and I'd like to compare reference-photo and perspective habits with other artists.
I say yes to extra work too fast and then pay for it with my body. I'd like to learn how other freelancers set limits.
My hands and wrists are overworked from long inking days. I want a more sustainable way to do this job for the next ten years.
Money is tight and rent depends on piece-rate pages. I'd like extra income that is less hard on my hands.
I feel lonely working as a freelancer in the studio and don't have real colleagues. I'd like peers I can talk to about the work.
I'm anxious about whether I can keep drawing for a living into my 30s.

offers.text: I ink dense city backgrounds, interiors and crowds for webtoons in Clip Studio Paint. When I'm well, I do about 6 pages of busy street scenes a week.
I have my own library of perspective grids and 3D room assets for Clip Studio, and I can lay out perspective for other artists.
I have a portfolio of 24 background boards and 8 short comics.
I can explain how to set up one-, two- and three-point perspective grids for comic backgrounds, in a short session or a written walkthrough.
I take reference photos of Seoul buildings, streets and riverside scenes, and can share them or shoot specific locations.
I know how a webtoon studio's freelance pool works: weekly deadlines, per-page chapter workflow, and how backgrounds are handed to a lead artist.
I know the Hongdae and Sangsu indie gig scene and can suggest venues, bands and where to eat afterward.
I can offer Korean-language help, such as talking through Seoul life, in exchange for English conversation practice.

catchers.hypo: Hi, I'm writing and directing an indie comic or visual novel set in a city, and I need a background artist for a few scenes. Can you take on a small paid job?
catchers.can: Take small paid background commissions, though my capacity is limited. Deliver inked streets and interiors from my own perspective grids and 3D room assets.
catchers.confirm: Is this a paid job with a clear page count and deadline, and not a long unpaid collaboration?

catchers.hypo: Hi, our small band plays Hongdae shows and we'd like an illustrator for a gig poster or cover art with a city-night feel.
catchers.can: Draw a night-street or interior-style poster illustration and bring my experience of the Hongdae gig scene.
catchers.confirm: Do you need a single illustrated poster or cover with a fixed fee and a few weeks of lead time, and not a long ongoing design contract?

catchers.hypo: Hi, I'm a Korean learner or native English speaker looking for a language partner who reads comics and shows with subtitles.
catchers.can: Do regular English and Korean exchange, and read comics in English together.
catchers.confirm: Are you after a regular, low-pressure exchange of about an hour a week, and not intensive paid tutoring?

catchers.hypo: Hi, I'm a writer, colorist or letterer, and I'd like to help finish a short comic about a night convenience store worker, trading help for credit.
catchers.can: Share my thumbnails and half-finished pencils, then co-finish the short with the right partner.
catchers.confirm: Are you able to help with a short of about 8 pages, with credit or a small fee, and can you work around a weekly deadline schedule?

catchers.hypo: Hi, I run a bakery or café and need illustrated interiors, menu art or packaging, and I know someone in Seoul who might help.
catchers.can: Through my roommate Mina, who works at a bakery, connect shops that need illustration, then draw interiors or menu art myself.
catchers.confirm: Is this a small commission for a real shop in Seoul, with a fixed brief and fee?

catchers.hypo: Hi, I'm putting together a team for a webtoon and need a background assistant who can match a lead artist's line quality.
catchers.can: Introduce them to my lead artist, if she is open to it, or take the work myself if the schedule fits.
catchers.confirm: Is the work per-page paid and on a regular weekly delivery cycle, and not a fixed-salary full-time job?

catchers.hypo: Hi, I work with illustrators and comic artists on healthy working habits for hands and wrists. I'm offering a session or a routine for people who draw long hours.
catchers.can: Try an ergonomic routine and learn how others keep drawing for decades, then share what works with my lead artist and colleagues.
catchers.confirm: Is your offer aimed at artists who draw long hours, available online or in Seoul, and affordable for a freelancer?

catchers.hypo: Hi, I'm a freelance artist who has set boundaries with studios on extra work and deadlines. Want to compare notes?
catchers.can: Compare experiences, and practice saying no or negotiating pages and deadlines.
catchers.confirm: Are you a working freelance comic or illustration artist who has negotiated workload with a studio?

forbids.text: I can't take on large unpaid projects, and I don't do free spec work beyond a small sample.
I can't commit to weekend work or tight deadlines during chapter weeks.
I can't take extended unpaid leave from my contract work.
I'm not willing to relocate away from Seoul.
I won't take on more pages than I can finish while looking after my hands.

projects.name: Night convenience store short
projects.text: An 8-page quiet comic about a girl who works at a night convenience store in Mapo. Thumbnails are done and pencils are half done.

policy.t1: Deadline routines, wanting to improve my English, interest in indie gigs, my own short comic and who could help with it, and my background and perspective offers.
policy.t2: Hand and wrist strain in general terms, money pressure, loneliness at work, and anxiety about my long-term career.
policy.never: Medical details, contract amounts, and family conflicts.
